This cheap and small model should also accept low reasoning'. A replay of six captured STM requests at reasoning low and a 2,048-token output (scratchpad, counts only): gpt-oss:20b 6/6 recorded, 136-774 output tokens, 2-5 s; glm-5.3-flash 6/6; inkling-2-small 6/6; qwen3.8-flash 5/6 (up to 1,787 reasoning tokens); mimo-v2.6-flash 5/6 (one at the cap); minimax-m3.1-flash and deepseek-v4.1-flash 6/6 with 1,000-1,300 reasoning tokens on some calls. Every arm's memory workers (STM, WM, LLM compaction summaries, Mem0) run on it; the main agent stays on hy4-flash-free. Owner, 2026-11-21 ('stop the arm and rerun the whole thing. You should use Muse Spark Contributor-1.3 as the worker model. Check if it supports low thinking first'): rule aff9613b stopped at 69/264 rows when Ollama Cloud answered 429 'monthly usage limit' to every gpt-oss:20b call from about 09:30Z (STM-only sb-id-01/02/03/16 were written from fallback records alone). muse-spark-1.3-contributor on OpenCode Go: catalog effort minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh, and a live probe (scratchpad, counts only: one arithmetic task, two pairs) spent 1,147 and 1,530 output tokens at low against 2,353 and 3,045 at high, so low reaches the model
rule.workerFaults: owner, 2026-11-21 ('worker failure is not a valid finding and defeats the purpose of the screen entirely'): a job with any memory-worker call that failed after every retry and wait (meter.workerErrors), or any STM batch recorded without the model (meter.stmFallbacks), leaves no row and runs again from its start after the fault wait; a third worker fault of one job stops the run for the owner; a provider's usage-limit answer (402/403/429 naming a usage, credit or quota limit) is never waited out and stops the run
rule.modelChoice: owner, 2026-11-19, at the launch approval: "use hy4 flash free model from opencode go instead of deepseek-v4.1-flash"; every arm and every memory worker on it. OpenCode Go's live catalog: 1,048,576 context (983,040 input), 65,536 output, price 0 (Prism's opencode-go provider has no static row for it and falls back to 200K; the harness window W is the same for every arm either way). Task 11's live guardrails were measured on deepseek-v4.1-flash, so the calibration stage re-checks them on this model (owner, 2026-11-19)
rule.workerSamplingNote: owner, 2026-11-20: workerReasoningEffort low is the default of every arm's memory-worker calls that set no effort of their own (a worker's own level wins, so STM's retry with thinking off reaches the wire); workerOutput window: a worker call may write what W leaves after its input (as a provider serving a W-token model allows), the main agent keeps the 2,048-token reserve. Found 2026-11-20: on rule 1a22763d hy4-flash-free ignored low and about 90% of STM worker calls (and memory-off-llm's summary calls) spent the whole 2,048 output reasoning, so the verdict measured a broken worker
rule.toolCallsPerTurnNote: owner, 2026-11-19 ("Pause; harness enforces one call per round"): hy4-flash-free ignores parallel_tool_calls:false (a scratchpad diagnostic on sb-rt-11 saw main-agent turns of 2 and 4 calls, e.g. a 3K file and a 17K artifact together), and Session-Bench assumes one artifact per round. The harness runs only the first tool call of each main-agent turn and answers the others with a fixed text (DEFERRED_TOOL_CALL_TEXT), for every arm alike; memory workers keep parallel calls; the model's output is never changed. Rule 77d8c3d4 was paused at 79/228 rows; its screen rows are superseded
rule.oracleWindow: oracle-context's 1,000,000 (the model's window): no session compacts
rule.samplingModelNote: thinkingLevel low is kept for equal treatment with Task 11's rule; Prism's catalog row for hy4-flash-free declares no reasoning-effort family, so the provider sends no effort and the model runs at its own default, the same for every arm
rule.samplingNote: temperature 0 for every call; the agent at thinkingLevel low (the memory workers' own default since gate M-2), so the 2,048-token output reserve is not spent thinking; Mem0's calls at low too; parallel_tool_calls false on the main agent's requests only, those that carry the workspace tools (owner, 2026-11-18, after the v2 smoke: DeepSeek read two ~18K artifacts in one round, over W, and no compaction can shrink fresh tool results; the benchmark assumes one artifact per round). Memory workers keep parallel calls: STM and WM record and judge through several tool calls in one turn and end after one clean turn (owner, 2026-11-18, after the first version of this rule sent the flag to every request with tools and STM recorded one event per batch)
rule.limitsNote: owner, 2026-11-19 ("Raise maxToolCalls for all arms"): the kernel charges maxToolCalls at dispatch, so a deferred call (one tool call per turn) uses a slot; maxToolCalls goes from 30 to 60 for every arm. productFixes.change: an STM source batch takes at most half the worker model's input cap (a larger entry is cut with its marker); recall { query } and recall { cursor } at summary detail stay within the page bytes; a compaction reads STM coverage recorded past its snapshot as covering the snapshot; recall { entry } carries its page once (the value doubled it); harness: one tool call per main-agent turn covers memory-package tools (recall) through tool.call respond, not only the workspace tools
productFixes.reason: owner, 2026-11-19 ('Run the diagnostic', then 'Go ahead and fix it'): rule 59864e7c's early check (41/63 STM-only task runs over W) and a counts-only diagnostic of sb-sc-18 showed (1) one ~60K-character tool result sent whole to the STM worker overflowed it on every pass, so coverage never moved and every later task failed; (2) recall answers of 180K-214K characters; (3) a background STM pass in flight at a mid-loop compaction recorded coverage past the snapshot, read as none, so the compaction declined and the next request overflowed; (4) the validation of those fixes (sb-sc-18: 10/11 tasks completed, 0 worker overflows) overflowed once, on three ~33K-character recall entry pages in one turn

productFixes.change: an STM source batch keeps a tool call with its results (an oversized result travels with its call, cut to fit); a background pass leaves an unanswered tool call for the next pass; a batch without the user's request carries it as context (no entry id); a record citing a tool call also cites its results; a cut recall page names how to read the entry whole
productFixes.reason: owner, 2026-11-20 ('investigate the reasons', then 'Do the proposed fixes'): rule 1a22763d finished with STM-only at 187/384 tasks against memory-off-llm's 206/384; a paired diagnostic (sb-rt-11, sb-sc-18, counts only) showed STM batches that split a call from its output, background passes run before the output existed, and batches that never showed the request they served

productFixes.change: an STM pass whose model ends at its output cap before any call is asked once more with thinking off; a second miss records the batch without the model (one bounded event per request, assistant text and tool call, marked fallback output_cap, citing the entries); a compaction's coverage pass whose model fails records the batch the same way (fallback worker_error) instead of declining
productFixes.reason: owner, 2026-11-20 ('How can we fix this?', then 'Build all three'): a worker model that ignores a low reasoning setting left STM with nothing recorded and the window full; the product must hold whatever the host's worker model does. analysis.unit: per check (dependency) or per task (task, control), paired by id; sessions are the clusters
analysis.statistic: pairedClusterPermutation (scripts/memory-bench/stats.mjs): cluster bootstrap 95% interval of the mean paired difference, sign-flip p
analysis.dependency: D1-D4 checks pooled (Session-Bench v3: the D4 check requires the new value only)
analysis.reported: every arm's scores, the pre-registered comparisons (score.mjs ANALYSIS), each decision arm against each side arm (sideComparisons) with the same statistic, cost per passed task, and the effect detectable at N

stm.text: STM is worth shipping if STM-only beats memory-off-llm on dependency checks (95% interval lower bound > 0) and is not worse on control checks (lower bound of the C difference > -0.05)

wm.text: WM's model policy is the default under a host scope only if STM+WM beats STM-only on dependency checks (lower bound > 0) and its whole-run input tokens per passed task are at most 1.5x STM-only's; otherwise the deterministic policy is the default (without a scope the session is STM-only)
wm.cost: whole-run input tokens (main + workers + embeddings, cached included) / tasks passed

decision.side: a Prism decision arm below a side arm (the side arm's 95% interval of the difference entirely above 0 on task or dependency checks) goes to the owner as a finding

detectable.method: (z_0.975 + z_0.8) x sd of per-session paired dependency-rate differences / sqrt(N), from this run's sessions
detectable.task11: at N = 36, about 23 points (memory-off-llm -> STM-only) and 8-12 points (STM-only -> STM+WM), from Task 11's 6 sessions
